I appreciate that you've been open to my directness and that we treat each other with respect. However, I don't view honesty as something to be traded or compromised on as a favor. Listening respectfully to differing opinions is the baseline of a healthy conversation, not a currency to buy agreement later.

If I look at your project plan, I'm more than happy to highlight what is actually working well and give credit where it's due. If it truly looks solid overall, I will tell you that. 

What I won't do is give you a blanket stamp of approval before I've even seen it, or pretend a major flaw doesn't exist just to spare your feelings. Calling something "solid" when it has serious gaps isn't just focusing on the positives—it is lying by omission. If you want to share the plan, I'll look at it fairly and point out its strengths, deal? But I can't promise to stay silent if I see something that's going to trip you up.
